lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.quote: A filing system treats each part of a dotted code as a separate integer subcode and files in ascending order. Which code comes first: $12.05$, $12.1$, or $12.008$?
lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.note: The dotted-code passage now asks a question and gives its answer in a separate numbered solution.

lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.quote: Arrange March $15$, $2024$; January $20$, $2024$; November $5$, $2023$; and February $10$, $2025$ from oldest to newest.
lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.note: Every date number in this revised question uses inline math.

lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.quote: Compare the next subcodes as whole numbers: $5$, $1$, and $8$.
lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.note: Dotted codes and the prose subcode numbers now use math delimiters instead of code spans or bare numbers.

lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.quote: The format keeps the date parts in the same places.
lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.note: The long lexicographic-order sentence has been replaced with short explanations of date parts and filing direction.

lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.quote: A period or hyphen inside a code may separate parts.
lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.note: The abstract identifier sentence is replaced with plain wording and local definitions of the two comparison methods.

lesson-clerical-ability-numeric-and-chro.quote: 1. Add ending zeros so all entries show the same number of decimal places.

reasoning-clerical-ability#21.quote: The fixed date format **YYYY-MM-DD** puts the year first, the month second, and the day last.
reasoning-clerical-ability#21.note: The lesson identifies all components, explains their digit widths, and applies the notation in Example #4.

reasoning-clerical-ability#24.quote: The first pair that differs decides the order.
reasoning-clerical-ability#24.note: The local character comparison procedure is taught and applied to A-10 and A-2 in Example #7.

reasoning-clerical-ability#25.quote: If the rule compares each number part as a whole number, compare the first part, then the second, and so on.
reasoning-clerical-ability#25.note: Hyphenated whole-number parts receive a local procedure and a worked tied-prefix comparison in Example #8.

reasoning-clerical-ability#26.quote: Move to the next group only when the groups you just checked match.
reasoning-clerical-ability#26.note: Terminal-digit filing is taught locally and Example #9 applies rightmost, middle, and leftmost tie comparisons.
